title: show bgp update-delay
text: show bgp update-delay Show the startup convergence hold and what it waits for. Ze command Registry path: show bgp update-delay Usage: show bgp update-delay Mode: Read-only Wire method: ze-bgp:update-delay Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: doc Address fields: none Column order: configured, holding, released, reason, expected-peers, peers-held, peers-converged, max-delay-seconds, establish-wait-seconds Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, on its rows: none Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none The command takes no argument, because the hold belongs to the speaker and not to a peer. configured says an operator set bgp update-delay max-delay. holding says this speaker is withholding its first advertisement right now, and released says the hold has ended. reason names the condition that ended it: converged, establish-wait or max-delay. expected-peers, peers-held and peers-converged say what the hold is still waiting for, so you can name the neighbor that has not finished. Read this command when a speaker has come up and advertised nothing: it separates a hold that is working from a daemon that is wedged. Arguments No command-specific arguments listed. text: show crashes View saved crash reports, and whether kernel capture is armed. title: show mtu

The run changes nothing on the router. With host <address>, one address is measured instead of the peers. Arguments Name Type Required Values Summary Description host union no any value of this type Measure one address instead of the IPsec peers. A name is refused: the run sends probes to the address as typed. search enum no exhaustive exhaustive: a slower run that probes every size and discards the cached and reported path MTU. text: show plugin conformance run Start a program in declare mode and check it behaves as a plugin. Ze command Registry path: show plugin conformance run Usage: show plugin conformance run <command> [name <name>] Mode: read-only, offline Wire method: ze-plugin:show-conformance-run Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: tab Address fields: none Column order: check, stage, verdict, reason, fix Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save, match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, on its rows: none Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none The program is started in declare mode, the way 'show plugin declarations' starts a configured plugin, and what it writes is judged with the checks the daemon applies at Stage 1. One row is written for each check: its name, the stage it belongs to, a verdict of pass, fail or not-judged, the reason, and the change that fixes a failure. A behavior this version does not judge keeps its row with the verdict not-judged, so an answer with no failure is not full conformance. The command exits 1 when a check failed. It runs in your own ze process only: the daemon starts no program a remote caller names, and answers with the command to run in your own shell. title: show probe-round
text: show probe-round Run a parallel traceroute probe round to a target. Ze command Registry path: show probe-round Usage: show probe-round [dest <dest>] [probes <probes>] [max-hops <max-hops>] [timeout <timeout>] Mode: Read-only Wire method: ze-traceroute:show-probe-round Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Sends all probes concurrently for faster results than sequential traceroute. Returns per-hop RTT and IP. Use probes and max-hops to tune accuracy vs speed. Arguments Name Type Required Values Summary Description dest string no any value of this type Target host or IP address. The value is the first bare word of the command. A host name is resolved in either address family, and the family of the answer selects ICMPv4 or ICMPv6. probes uint no any value of this type Number of probes per hop. The value is accepted in the range 1 to 10 and then not read: a probe round sends one probe at each time-to-live. max-hops uint no any value of this type Maximum number of hops. The value is the largest time-to-live Ze probes, 1 to 64. Absent, or set to 30, the round probes 16 hops. timeout string no any value of this type Timeout duration. The value is accepted in Go duration s

text: show system dns Learned DNS resolvers and each consumer's dns-source selection. Ze command Registry path: show system dns Usage: show system dns Mode: Read-only Wire method: ze-system-dns:show-system-dns Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none The answer lists every learned resolver record (its origin, interface, unit, addresses, when it was received and when it expires), then every dns-source consumer's selection: the router's own under the consumer name system, and each consumer that published one (the LAN resolver, each DHCP subnet, each RA unit, each subscriber pool). Each selection carries its config path, the instance it belongs to, the sources and mode evaluated, default true while the built-in default list applies, the classes used and the servers handed on. A consumer that has not published yet is absent: its plugin is not running or has not received the first snapshot. A plugin removed while the daemon runs withdraws its selection, so it is absent too. title: show traceroute
text: show traceroute Trace the network path from this router to a target. Ze command Registry path: show traceroute Usage: show traceroute [dest <dest>] [max-hops <max-hops>] [timeout <timeout>] [probes <probes>] [do-not-fragment <honor-cache|bypass-cache>] Mode: read-only, offline Wire method: ze-traceroute:show-traceroute Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Shows each hop with its IP and round-trip time. Dest can be an IP or hostname. Defaults: 30 max hops, 3 probes per hop. Increase probes for more reliable RTT measurements. Arguments Name Type Required Values Summary Description dest string no any value of this type Target host or IP address. The value is the first bare word of the command. A host name is resolved in either address family, and the family of the answer selects ICMPv4 or ICMPv6. max-hops uint no any value of this type Maximum number of hops. The value is the largest time-to-live Ze probes, 1 to 64. The trace stops early when the target answers. Absent, the value is 30. timeout string no any value of this type Timeout duration. The value is the time Ze waits for one probe, in Go duration syntax, 1s to 30s. Absent, the value is 3s. probes uint no any

title: show vpn ipsec dataplane policy
text: show vpn ipsec dataplane policy Show the Security Policy Database the kernel holds. Ze command Registry path: show vpn ipsec dataplane policy Usage: show vpn ipsec dataplane policy Mode: Read-only Wire method: ze-ike:show-vpn-ipsec-dataplane-policy Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Lists each policy with its selector prefixes and ports, direction, priority, upper-layer protocol, if_id, interface index, tunnel endpoints, and the peer that installed it. Each policy also names the SPD that holds it (spd: node for if_id 0, the bound XFRM interface, or if-id and the number) and the job Ze installed it for (role), which reads unknown for a policy Ze did not install. A per-socket policy, which overrides every SPD entry for its one socket, reads spd socket, its direction in, out or fwd, and role esp-form-socket for Ze's own ESP form reader or socket-override for any other process's. A policy with no matching SA is the failure this command exists to show. RFC 4301 Section 4.4 keeps the SPD and the SAD separate, and so does this tree. title: update bgp config
text: update bgp config Write the running peer set to the configuration file. Ze command Registry path: update bgp config Usage: update bgp config Mode: Daemon Wire method: ze-bgp:peer-save Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: doc Address fields: none Column order: added, removed, config, message Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, on its rows: none Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Ze writes the running peer set into the configuration file. A peer 'create bgp peer' built is added to the file, and a peer the file declares that 'delete bgp peer' removed is taken out of it. A peer both sides already hold is left exactly as it was written. The running daemon does not change: the file is brought to it. The command takes no selector, because after a delete no peer is left to name and that absence is half of what the command persists. A created peer is written under a name derived from its address, such as 'peer-192.0.2.7', because a peer name cannot start with a digit. The answer names what was added, what was removed, and the file that was written. Arguments No command-specific arguments listed. title: update data config
text: update data config Import one config into the daemon's store as a new version. Ze command Registry path: update data config Usage: update data config <name> content <content> Mode: Daemon Wire method: ze-config:data-config-update Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Imports one config through the store the daemon owns, so it works while ze runs. For the daemon's own config, the content is staged as the candidate and the same reload a SIGHUP runs promotes it: the config becomes active only when the reload accepts it, and a refused config leaves the active config, its pointers and the daemon unchanged, with the reload's reason in the refusal. The import is refused while a confirmed-commit window is open, with the window's own refusal, and while another change is staged. For any other name, the content is committed as a new active version, the previous one kept as rollback, and nothing reloads. The answer carries the name, the version stamp and the byte count. The content is never recorded: the audit log, the accounting record, the SSH exec log and the session transcript hold a placeholder in its place. Arguments Name Type Required Values Summary Description name str

title: update data key
text: update data key Write one runtime-state key into the daemon's store. Ze command Registry path: update data key Usage: update data key <key> content <content> Mode: Daemon Wire method: ze-config:data-key-update Backends: any backend Task support: optional: the MCP call is synchronous, which is the default Subcommands: none: this command takes no subcommand Answer shape: not declared Address fields: none Column order: none Pipes, always: json, ndjson, table, text, yaml, raw, no-more, save Pipes, when the answer has rows: match, count, first, last, display, fill Pipes, while streaming: log Pipes, local process only: save Command pipes: none Pipe aliases: none Writes one runtime-state key (a key under meta/ outside meta/config/) through the store the daemon owns, so it works while ze runs. The key is created, or replaced when it exists, with the bytes content decodes to, and the answer carries the key and the byte count. A configuration key (under file/ or meta/config/, or outside both) is refused before the store is touched, because a raw write bypasses its versions, pointers and history. A key a plugin is granted is refused while that plugin runs, because the plugin manages the key while it runs; the refusal names the plugin and its restart. Until the daemon has started its plugins, such a key is refused, because the daemon cannot tell yet whether the plugin runs. The content is never recorded: the audit log, the accounting record, the SSH exec log and the session transcript hold a placeholder in its place. Arguments Name Type Required Values Summary Description key string ye

A daemon runs one such server at a time. Through the daemon, 'update serve' alone answers that server's status: whether it runs, the address it listens on and whether it is paused. The foreground 'ze update serve', given the address to listen on, runs the same server in the operator's own process instead. Arguments No command-specific arguments listed. title: anomaly
text: anomaly detect baseline-window uint32 clear-consecutive uint8 cohort-prefix-len-v4 uint8 cohort-prefix-len-v6 uint8 confirm-duration uint16 corroboration-weight decimal-2 deviation-threshold decimal-2 enabled boolean min-cohort-size uint16 min-features-to-correlate uint8 observe incident-ring-size uint32 stale-incident-timeout uint32 shape action enumeration allowlist ip-prefix auto-revert-ttl uint16 blast-radius-cap uint16 kill-switch boolean limit-burst uint32 limit-rate uint64 limit-unit enumeration mode enumeration Behavioral anomaly detection and response subsystem. Two plugins fill this container. anomaly-detect owns the detect subtree and reports incidents on the event bus. anomaly-shape adds the shape subtree and acts on those incidents. Remove a plugin and its subtree disappears from the config. Report-only behavioral anomaly detector (emits incidents, takes no action). The detector reads one traffic-feature snapshot every second, and one second is one tick. It holds a baseline for each entity on three axes: the source address, the destination address, and the port. It publishes an incident on the event bus, and it writes no firewall rule. The shape subtree is what acts on an incident. Per-entity baseline horizon in ticks (the EWMA smoothing factor is derived from it). Ze derives the EWMA smoothing factor from this window: alpha is 2 divided by the window plus 1. The default 300 gives an alpha of 0.0066. A longer window makes the baseline slower and a short burst more visible. Ze folds a tick into the baseline only when the entity is not anomalous on that tick. A long anomaly cannot drift the baseline up to meet it. Consecutive below-threshold ticks before an active incident clears. One tick is one second. An active incident clears after this many ticks in a row below the threshold, and one tick above it resets the count to 0. The default 10 holds the incident for 10 seconds after the traffic stops. Source-prefix length that buckets IPv4 entities into peer-group cohorts. Ze masks the IPv4 address of the entity to this length and uses the result as the cohort key. Ze compares each entity against the other members of its cohort, which is how it scores rarity. A shorter length makes a larger cohort. min-cohort-size sets the smallest cohort Ze scores rarity in. Source-prefix length that buckets IPv6 entities into peer-group cohorts. Ze masks the IPv6 address of the entity to this length and uses the result as the cohort key. The default 48 groups a site together. Where the mask does not apply to the address, Ze falls back to the whole address. That entity then forms a cohort of one, and Ze scores it on its own baseline alone. Consecutive above-threshold ticks before an incident is confirmed and emitted. One tick is one second. Ze needs this many ticks in a row above the threshold, and one tick below it resets the count to 0. The default 3 delays an incident by 3 seconds and it drops a one-tick spike. Discount applied to a corroborating feature when Ze combines scores. Discount applied to corroborating features when combining scores. The discount stops correlated features from counting twice. Sigma at or above which a per-entity feature deviation fires. A feature fires when its z-score reaches this value. That score is the larger of two numbers. The first is the deviation from the entity own baseline. The second is the rarity of the value in the cohort of the entity. A lower value fires more features and raises the number of false incidents. The value also grades the severity Ze puts on an incident. Enable the behavioral anomaly detector (report-only; emits incidents, takes no action). The default false leaves the detector idle: it starts no ticker and it holds no baseline. Set it true and Ze attaches to the traffic-feature service and starts the one-second ticker. An entity needs 3 ticks of samples before Ze scores its deviation from its own baseline. Minimum members in a cohort before Ze scores peer-group rarity. Minimum cohort members before peer-group rarity is scored. A cohort is a source-prefix bucket. A smaller cohort uses self-deviation only. Minimum distinct features that must fire before Ze scores an incident. Minimum distinct features that must fire on one entity and one window before Ze scores an incident. The minimum correlates weak signals, so one feature alone raises no incident. Incident lifecycle store for confirmed anomaly incidents. The store keeps each confirmed incident from its start to its end. `show anomaly observe` reads the store, so it can report the duration of a finished incident. Maximum number of incidents the ring keeps in memory. When the ring is full, the oldest finalized incident is dropped first. Seconds before an open incident with no clear event is finalized. The detector stops reporting an entity that goes idle, and it sends no clear event for that entity. This timeout is the limit on how long such an incident reads as active. Autonomous responder: shadow (log-only) or armed (live per-source firewall actions). The responder reads the incidents the detect subtree publishes, and it acts on a source incident alone. In armed mode it writes an nftables table named ze_anomaly-shape, with one term for each armed source. The chain of that table attaches to the input hook at priority -200, so it acts on the traffic addressed to this host. Armed action: rate-limit the source (surgical) or drop it (fallback). limit writes an nftables counter and a rate limit on the source prefix, and it reads limit-rate, limit-unit and limit-burst. drop writes a counter and discards every packet from that source. Ze applies the action to each armed source, and it applies nothing while mode is shadow. Protected source prefixes that ze never arms an action against. The list guards against self-lockout, for management sources and control-plane sources. Seconds after the last signal before an armed action reverts by itself. This ceiling holds whether or not a clear event arrives, so an armed action can never stay in place indefinitely. Maximum concurrently-armed live actions; further arm attempts are refused. Ze counts the sources that carry a live action. At this cap Ze refuses to arm one more source, writes a warning, and raises the arm-refused metric. A source that is armed already costs the count nothing, because that path only refreshes its auto-revert-ttl. The cap bounds the firewall table an incident storm can produce. When true, revert every armed action and force the responder to shadow. Ze runs the revert when it reads the config, so it also removes what an earlier instance of the responder left in the firewall. The responder then answers every incident as shadow does, and it writes a log line in place of a rule. Set the leaf back to false to let the responder arm again. Burst allowance for the limit action. The burst is the number of packets Ze lets through above the rate before it starts to drop. The default 0 gives no allowance, so the rate applies from the first packet. Ze gives the value to the nftables limit expression. The leaf changes nothing while the action is drop. Rate for the limit action, in packets per limit-unit. The rate counts packets, and limit-unit gives the time. The default 1000, with the default unit second, lets 1000 packets a second through from each armed source. A value of 0 is refused at commit while the action is limit. The leaf changes nothing while the action is drop. Time unit for limit-rate. The unit divides limit-rate. A rate of 1000 with the unit minute lets 1000 packets a minute through. Ze gives the word to the nftables limit expression, and a word outside the four is refused at commit. The leaf changes nothing while the action is drop. Responder mode: shadow or armed. shadow, the default, logs the action it would take and installs nothing. armed installs live per-source firewall actions.

title: bfd
text: bfd bind-v6 boolean enabled boolean multi-hop-session <peer local vrf> local string min-ttl uint8 peer string profile leafref shutdown boolean vrf string persist-dir string profile <name> auth key-id uint8 secret-form secret secret string secret-hex secret-hex string type enumeration desired-min-tx-us uint32 detect-multiplier uint8 echo desired-min-echo-tx-us uint32 passive boolean required-min-rx-us uint32 single-hop-session <peer vrf interface> interface string local string peer string profile leafref shutdown boolean vrf string BFD control configuration for Ze. The container holds the plugin switch, the reusable profiles, and the sessions an operator pins. A session that BGP or a static route asks for at runtime does not appear here. A protocol client reaches the plugin through its Service interface instead. Bind an IPv6 socket beside the IPv4 socket on every loop. When this leaf is true, the BFD plugin also binds an IPv6 socket (::0) alongside the IPv4 socket for every (vrf, mode) loop. The paired sockets share the same RX channel through a transport.Dual wrapper, and send routes by destination address family. Stage 2b (spec-bfd-2b-ipv6-transport) ships this leaf. A pinned IPv6 session requires the leaf to be set explicitly, so an operator who does not need IPv6 does not open a second socket per loop. Master switch for the BFD plugin. The default is true. false stops every BFD session, the ones pinned in this bfd container and the ones a protocol client asks for at runtime. A reload to false stops the pinned sessions already running. A config that sets false while a BGP peer, a static next-hop or an OSPF interface still opts into BFD is refused, naming those clients, so remove the opt-ins first. To stop the session of one peer only, remove the bfd container from that peer or set its enabled leaf to false. Multi-hop BFD session (RFC 5883). Port 4784, no GTSM. The 255-TTL test of a single-hop session cannot work over several hops. The min-ttl leaf is the cheap protection here, and authentication is the strong one. Ze refuses an entry whose profile enables echo. RFC 5883 Section 3 states that the Echo function MUST NOT be used over multiple hops. The local leaf is required here, and it is optional on a single-hop session. Local source address. Required for multi-hop. Ze refuses an entry that omits this leaf. The address is the source of every Control packet Ze sends, and it is part of the session key. RFC 5883 Section 4.1 states that two sessions between the same pair of systems must differ in at least one endpoint address. The reason is that the first packet carries a Your Discriminator of 0. Minimum acceptable TTL on receive. Weak replacement for GTSM on multi-hop paths. Ze discards a Control packet whose TTL is less than this value, and the test is inclusive, so a TTL equal to it passes. A peer sends with a TTL of 255, so 254 allows one router between the peer and Ze. Raise the value toward 255 when the peer is fewer hops away, because a higher floor rejects a packet sent from further away. Address of the remote system this session runs to. The value is the first word after the list name, so multi-hop-session 203.0.113.9 names this peer. Ze refuses an address it cannot parse, and IPv4 and IPv6 are both accepted. The peer, the local address and the VRF together identify the session. Name of the timer profile this session takes its intervals from. Commit refuses a name that no profile declares, and names the profiles that exist. Ze also refuses a profile that enables echo. Without this leaf the session takes the engine values: a detect multiplier of 3, and 1000000 microseconds for both the transmit target and the receive floor. Hold the session administratively down and keep its configuration. The session stays configured and stops sending control packets, so a peer sees it go down. Delete the list entry to remove it instead. Routing instance the session runs in. The default instance is named default. A name other than default binds the socket to the VRF device of that name. Ze runs one socket for each pair of VRF and hop mode, so every multi-hop session in one VRF shares it. An empty value is refused: the leaf is part of the key. DEPRECATED. A non-empty value opts a session into sequence persistence. DEPRECATED, retained for back-compat and scheduled for removal. The value is no longer interpreted as a directory. TX sequence numbers for Meticulous Keyed authentication now persist to the shared managed store (the database/ tree), instead of a loose file. A non-empty value still opts a session into persistence. RFC 5880 Section 6.7.3 requires the sequence to survive process restarts. Without this leaf set, Meticulous sessions still work at runtime, but a fresh process loses its sequence floor until the peer's replay window slides forward. Reusable timer and feature profile. Reusable timer and feature profile. Sessions reference a profile by name and inherit every field below. Authentication parameters (RFC 5880 Section 6.7). RFC 5880 Section 6.7 authentication parameters. Sessions inheriting this profile sign every outgoing Control packet with the configured type, and verify incoming packets with the same key. There is no default type, and authentication runs only on the type the operator names here. Auth Key ID (RFC 5880 Section 6.7.1). Ze writes the value into the authentication section of every Control packet it sends. Ze discards a received packet that carries another value, which RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2 requires for Simple Password. Both ends must name the same key-id and the same secret. The range is 0 to 255. The shared secret, as an ASCII string or in hexadecimal. Name the shared secret in exactly one form. secret takes an ASCII string and uses its bytes as the key. secret-hex takes any binary string written in hexadecimal, so a key holding a zero byte or a byte above 0x7F can be configured (RFC 5880 Sections 6.7.2, 6.7.3 and 6.7.4). Ze refuses a profile that names both forms or neither. Shared secret as an ASCII string, redacted from `ze config show` output. Shared secret as an ASCII string, whose bytes are the key. Redacted from `ze config show` output. The MD5 variants take a secret of up to 16 bytes (RFC 5880 Section 6.7.3) and the SHA1 variants one of up to 20 bytes (Section 6.7.4). Both pad a shorter secret with zeros, and a longer one is refused at parse time. The simple-password type carries the secret itself on the wire, so it must be 1 to 16 bytes, and a longer one is refused at parse time too (RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2). Shared secret as hexadecimal digits, two for each byte, redacted from output. Shared secret as a binary string in hexadecimal, two digits for each byte with no 0x prefix, upper or lower case. Redacted from `ze config show` output. The decoded key obeys the same limits as secret: 1 to 16 bytes for simple-password, up to 16 bytes for the MD5 variants and up to 20 bytes for the SHA1 variants (RFC 5880 Sections 6.7.2, 6.7.3 and 6.7.4). Authentication type, which the operator must name. Authentication type. There is no default. The operator names the type, and simple-password is never selected on their behalf. simple-password is RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2 Simple Password. The password travels in clear in every Control packet and the section never changes, so it protects against a misconfigured peer and against nothing else. It does not protect against a listener on the path, who reads the password from one packet, and it carries no Sequence Number, so a captured packet can be replayed. Choose a keyed type wherever the path is not already trusted. Local target transmit rate in microseconds. Local target transmit rate in microseconds. The slow-start floor of 1 000 000 us applies while the session is not Up, per RFC 5880 Section 6.8.3. Consecutive missed Control packets that trigger a Down transition. Number of consecutive missed Control packets that trigger a Down transition. RFC 5880 Section 6.8.4. BFD Echo mode (RFC 5880 Section 6.4, RFC 5881 Section 5). RFC 5880 Section 6.4 / RFC 5881 Section 5 Echo mode. Echo mode is single-hop only, because RFC 5883 Section 3 prohibits multi-hop echo: a multi-hop session or BGP peer that uses an echo profile is refused. When echo is active, the engine sends echo packets on UDP port 3785 at the peer's advertised RequiredMinEchoRxInterval. The engine then slows its async Control TX to the peer's RequiredMinRxInterval. Local target echo transmit rate in microseconds. Local target echo transmit rate in microseconds. The effective echo rate is max(local desired, peer RequiredMinEchoRx). Wait for a peer Control packet before this session transmits. Active, which is the default, transmits from session creation. Passive transmits nothing until a Control packet arrives from the peer. RFC 5883 Section 4.3. A single-hop session, BGP peer or static next-hop that uses a passive profile is refused: RFC 5881 Section 3 requires the Active role on a single hop. Minimum inter-packet gap the local end can handle, in microseconds. Ze advertises the value as Required Min RX Interval, and a peer that obeys it does not transmit faster. The detection time is the peer's Detect Multiplier times the larger of this value and the peer's Desired Min TX Interval. While echo mode runs, Ze raises the advertised value to 1000000 microseconds and starts a Poll sequence, because the echo packets already prove the path. Per-link BFD session on port 3784 with TTL 255 (RFC 5881). Per-link BFD session (RFC 5881). Port 3784, TTL=255. A protocol client MUST NOT use this list. A protocol client calls the plugin Service interface at runtime. Egress interface name. Ze binds the socket of the loop to this interface with SO_BINDTODEVICE. One socket serves every session of one VRF and hop mode. Ze binds it only when each session in the default VRF names the same interface. A mix of names leaves the socket unbound, with a warning in the log. In a VRF other than default the VRF device wins, and this leaf is dropped from the socket binding; it still names the session's link. An IPv6 link-local peer needs this leaf in every VRF. Local source address (optional). While the leaf is absent, the kernel selects the source address. The address is part of the session key. A change to it therefore releases the running session, and creates a new one at the next config load. An address written with a zone is refused: the link is written in interface. Peer IPv4 or IPv6 address. The value is the first word after the list name, so single-hop-session 203.0.113.9 names this peer. Ze refuses an address it cannot parse, and IPv4 and IPv6 are both accepted. RFC 5881 Section 5 requires a received TTL of 255, so Ze discards a Control packet from this peer that crossed a router. An IPv6 link-local peer (fe80::/10) is refused unless the entry names its link in interface, and an address written with a zone (fe80::b%eth0) is refused: the link is written in interface. Named profile to inherit timer parameters from. Commit refuses a name that no profile declares, and names the profiles that exist. Without this leaf the session takes the engine values: a detect multiplier of 3, and 1000000 microseconds for both the transmit target and the receive floor. When true, the session stays in AdminDown state. RFC 5880 Section 6.8.16. The session keeps its configuration and its place in the list, and Ze holds it in AdminDown. Ze applies the value again at each reload, so a change from true to false brings the session back with no restart. Delete the list entry to remove the session instead. Routing instance the session runs in. The default instance is named default. A name other than default binds the socket to the VRF device of that name. The interface leaf of every session in that VRF is then dropped, and Ze logs the names it dropped once for each loop. An empty value is refused: the leaf is part of the key.

title: bgp-epe
text: bgp-epe peer <address> sid-index uint32 weight uint8 srgb lower-bound uint32 upper-bound uint32 Instantiate BGP Egress Peer Engineering segments. The internal bgp-epe plugin consumes state events from attached BGP sessions. Each configured peer gets a persistent PeerNode SID index. While its session is established, the corresponding local label is popped and forwarded to the peer by the selected MPLS FIB writer. State withdrawal removes that label and its BGP-LS advertisement. Configure bgp-ls-export to advertise the native state to collectors. This SRGB must be reserved exclusively for these EPE labels and must not overlap another label producer. BGP session whose connected peer is an EPE next hop. Assign one distinct SRGB index to each established session's remote peer. Removing an assignment removes its forwarding label and withdraws its native BGP-LS state. Persistent PeerNode SID index in the EPE SRGB. Unique offset into the configured SRGB. The assignment remains stable across process restart and session flap. PeerNode SID load-balancing weight. Relative load-balancing weight advertised in the PeerNode SID attribute. Reserve the local label range for EPE PeerNode segments. Local SRGB reserved for EPE PeerNode segments. First label in the EPE SRGB. Inclusive lower label bound; labels below 16 are reserved by MPLS. Last label in the EPE SRGB. Inclusive upper label bound, which must be at least the lower bound.

title: bgp-ls-export
text: bgp-ls-export domain <name> instance-id uint64 native-area uint32 native-instance uint64 protocol-id uint8 source string Export native routing state through BGP-LS. Export the running native IGP databases to BGP peers that attach this internal plugin with state/refresh receive and update send grants. Each database snapshot replaces prior node, link, prefix, and SRv6 SID advertisements. Removed identities are withdrawn before replacements. The exporter retains at most 65536 routes and refuses a replacement exceeding that bound without changing the last accepted database. This feature requires the in-process engine event bus; it does not originate from a forked plugin. Set the 64-bit BGP-LS Instance-ID of a native domain. Assign a routing-universe Instance-ID to one native domain. Unmapped domains retain the source's native identifier. Eight-octet routing-universe identifier. Full-width Instance-ID placed in originated NLRIs for the selected domain. Numeric source area or IS-IS level. Native numeric OSPF area or IS-IS level published by the source. Source instance identifier. Native instance number published by the selected routing protocol. BGP-LS source Protocol-ID. Protocol identifier of the native snapshot selected by this mapping. Native source namespace. Registered link-state publisher namespace, such as isis, ospf, or bgp-epe.

title: class-of-service
text: class-of-service ieee-802.1p <name> egress priority <value> pcp uint8 ingress pcp <value> priority uint8 Named class-of-service profiles. A profile maps the 3-bit PCP field of an 802.1Q header to an internal priority, in the ingress direction and in the egress direction. An interface leaf and a unit leaf name the profile they use. An 802.1p QoS profile. The profile defines the mapping between the 3-bit PCP field in the 802.1Q header and the internal priorities. It covers the ingress direction and the egress direction. Priority-to-PCP mapping of a transmitted tagged frame. Ze reads this mapping when it stamps the PCP field of a frame it transmits. Map one internal priority to a transmitted PCP value. The list key is the internal priority, so the list holds at most one entry for each of the eight priorities. PCP value Ze stamps in the 802.1Q header. IEEE 802.1Q defines the Priority Code Point field, which is 3 bits wide and holds a value from 0 to 7. PCP-to-priority mapping of a received tagged frame. Ze reads this mapping when it takes the internal priority of a frame it receives. Map one received PCP value to an internal priority. The list key is the PCP value, so the list holds at most one entry for each of the eight values. Internal priority Ze gives to a matching frame. The value runs from 0 to 7.

title: connected
text: connected filter import filters string final enumeration Connected route redistribution. Presence enables the plugin. The container carries no leaf, so writing it is the whole configuration. The plugin watches each interface address event and emits the network prefix of that address on the redistribute event bus. It counts the addresses of one prefix, so two addresses in one subnet announce the prefix once. The withdrawal waits for the last address of that prefix. The plugin registers the connected route source, and a redistribute statement names that source. Route filter chains into the Loc-RIB. A name references a filter instance defined under the top-level policy root. The chain judges routes as they enter the Loc-RIB. Import policy into the Loc-RIB A rejected route stays in the Loc-RIB as a hidden path that is never selected, so relaxing the chain re-admits it without the protocol sending it again. The source's chain runs first, then the rib chain. Ordered filter instance references Run these filter instances in order. Each one passes the route on or rejects it; a filter type with no Loc-RIB route evaluator is refused. Decision after every filter passes Every present import policy must set final accept or final reject, even with no filters.

title: container
text: container instance <name> enabled boolean image string network <name> address ip-address mac-address string port <name> container-port string protocol enumeration public-address ip-address public-port string stop-signal enumeration stop-timeout uint16 network <name> gateway ip-address masquerade boolean mtu uint16 prefix ip-prefix registry <name> authentication password string username string description string mirror address string path string port port transport enumeration Containers Ze runs from OCI images. A container is a workload Ze starts from an image and confines: its own namespaces, a limited control group, a reduced capability set and a system-call filter. Ze starts each configured container, restarts it under its policy and removes it when the configuration no longer holds it. A container Ze runs from an image. One entry is one container. Whether it runs is stated here and nowhere else: Ze has no start command and no stop command, and the enabled leaf says whether the container runs. Run this container; false keeps its config and stops it. The default is true. False keeps every other statement of the container in the configuration and keeps the container stopped, in the disabled state, until the leaf is true again. Image name; a short name is looked up on Docker Hub, and no tag means latest. The image the container runs: a short name, which completes on the public hub with the library prefix for a one-word name, a whole reference with its registry host, or a reference by sha256 digest. A reference with no tag and no digest takes the tag latest. The image store must hold the image: create container image reference fetches it, and a container whose image is absent waits for it. Attachment to a container network. One entry attaches the container to one container network. The container gets one link per entry, named eth0, eth1 and on in the order the entries are written. An absent address is assigned and an absent mac-address is derived; neither is written to the configuration. Address of the container on the network. At most one address per address family, inside the network's prefix, and not its network, broadcast or gateway address. A family with no address set is assigned the lowest free one, and the assignment stays the same across restarts. Hardware address of the container's end of the link. When absent, a locally administered address is derived from the network and container names, so it is the same at every start. Port of the router that reaches a port of the container. One entry publishes a port of the container on the router: a connection to an address of the router on the public port is translated to the container's address on its first network and the container port. Only traffic addressed to the router is translated, never traffic the router forwards. The operator's firewall policy must also allow the translated traffic. Port of the container the connection reaches. One port, or a first-last range, of the same length as the public port. A range is published onto the same range. Transport protocol of the published port. The transport protocol the port is published for. Address of the router the port is published on. The addresses of the router the port is published on. When none is set, every address of the router is, in each family the container has an address of on its first network. Port of the router that is published. One port, or a first-last range, from 1 to 65535. Signal that asks the container to stop. The signal a stop sends to the container's first process. When the leaf is absent, the signal the image declares is sent, or the termination signal when the image declares none. Time between the stop signal and the kill. A stop sends the container its stop signal, then waits this long for it to end before Ze kills every process of it through its control group. The top of the range is 30 because a daemon stop gives the containers 30 seconds to obey their stop signals. A network that containers attach to. One entry is one container network: a bridge device named zcn- plus the name, holding the gateway address of each prefix. Each attached container has one link whose host end is a member of the bridge. Address of the router on the network. At most one per prefix, a host address of it. When absent, the gateway of a prefix is its first host address. Translate outbound traffic to the router's address. True translates traffic leaving the network through another interface to the router's address on that interface. Traffic between two containers of the network keeps its source. Largest packet the network carries. Set on the bridge and on both ends of every link. A network with an IPv6 prefix needs at least 1280. Address range of the network, one per address family. At most one prefix per address family. An IPv4 prefix has a length of 1 to 30 and an IPv6 prefix 1 to 126, and two networks must not overlap. Settings for one image registry. One entry holds the settings of one image registry. A registry with no entry is reached over HTTPS, verified through the system roots, with no credentials and no mirror. The public hub needs no entry; an entry named docker.io gives it a mirror or credentials like any other registry. A change applies to the next fetch. Credentials Ze presents to the registry. The credentials are sent to the registry or to the token realm it names, and never to the mirror. Both leaves are mandatory. Password or access token on the registry. The password or access token of the account. Every display of the configuration masks it. User name on the registry. The user name of the account on the registry. Free text shown with the registry. Free text for the operator. Ze does not interpret it. Server Ze asks first; the registry is asked when it fails. One mirror for the registry. Every manifest and blob is asked of the mirror first, once and with no credentials, and of the registry when the mirror fails in any way. What the mirror serves passes the same digest and size checks. IP address or host name of the mirror. An IP address or a host name in lower case. A loopback address is accepted. Path prefix of the mirror, starting with a slash. The path the mirror serves the registry protocol under. It starts with one slash, never two, holds no backslash, and is placed before the /v2/ path of every request to the mirror. Port of the mirror. The default is 443 whatever the transport, so a mirror reached over http names its port. Protocol Ze speaks to the registry and to its mirror. The protocol applies to the registry and to its mirror. Over https the server's certificate is always verified: there is no unverified form.

title: control-plane-protection
text: control-plane-protection bgp burst uint32 over-limit-policy enumeration protected-port uint16 rate rate-spec trusted-source string Control-plane policing configuration. Ze compiles the containers under it into one nftables table named ze_copp, which carries a base input chain at priority 0. The ze_ prefix is what makes the firewall backend own that table and withdraw it when you delete the configuration. The bgp container is the only policy Ze builds today. Accept BGP connections from configured neighbors only, and drop the rest. An access list on TCP to the protected ports (RFC 7454 Section 4). Ze accepts an established or related connection first, then a connection from each trusted-source prefix, then a connection from a configured BGP neighbor: the remote ip of each static peer and the range of each dynamic group, read from the bgp configuration. Ze counts and drops TCP to a protected port from every other source. The rate, when set, limits new connections from the neighbors only. Ze builds the table when you write the container and removes it when you delete the container. A configuration without this container gets no access list. Burst size (packets or bytes matching the rate unit). The unit follows the unit of rate: a packet count where rate counts packets, and a byte count where rate names a byte unit. The leaf has no default, and Ze gives the kernel a burst of 0 when it is absent. Ze refuses a burst without a rate. What Ze does with neighbor connections that exceed the rate limit. drop, the default, discards a new connection from a BGP neighbor once the rate is exceeded. accept lets those connections through, so the limit reports load and stops nothing; use it to observe a new rate before you enforce it. The leaf matters only when rate is set, and it never changes the access list: a source that is not a neighbor is dropped under either setting. The input chain keeps an accept policy, so SSH, ICMP and every service this table never names stay reachable, and an established session is accepted before the limit is read. TCP port(s) the control-plane policing rules protect, 179 (BGP) by default. TCP port(s) to protect. Ze uses 179, the BGP port, when this leaf is omitted. Set a different value when the BGP listener uses another port. Limit for new connections from BGP neighbors (e.g., 100/second). The leaf is optional. Without it Ze builds the access list and no limit. The value is a count, an optional byte unit, and a time unit, as in 100/second or 1mbytes/second. The limit applies to new TCP connections from configured BGP neighbors. A trusted-source prefix and an established session never meet it, and a source that is not a neighbor is dropped before it. Source prefixes accepted without being BGP neighbors, and never rate limited. Ze adds one accept term for each prefix, ahead of the neighbor terms. The term matches TCP from that source to a protected port, so a trusted source is never dropped and never meets the rate limit. Use it for a source that is not a configured BGP neighbor, such as a monitoring host. Ze refuses a value that is not an IPv4 prefix or an IPv6 prefix.

title: ddos
text: ddos detect absolute-floor uint32 baseline-window uint32 bps-floor uint64 bps-threshold-multiplier decimal-2 bps-trigger-enable boolean characterize-enable boolean characterize-timeout uint16 characterize-window uint16 check-interval uint16 clear-consecutive-checks uint16 confirm-duration uint16 enabled boolean entropy-threshold decimal-2 policy default-action enumeration rule <prefix> action enumeration match enumeration scope enumeration startup-grace uint16 threshold-multiplier decimal-2 top-n-sources uint16 flowspec action enumeration announce-rate-limit uint16 backoff-cap uint32 blackhole-fallback boolean confidence-min uint8 hold-down uint32 max-mitigation-duration uint32 probe-interval uint16 probe-rate uint32 probe-window uint16 rate-limit-bytes uint64 response-level enumeration flowtriq api-base string api-key string enabled boolean node-uuid string local confidence-min uint8 forward-mitigation boolean max-mitigation-duration uint32 response-level enumeration observe incident-ring-size uint32 stale-incident-timeout uint32 Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem. Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem. This module declares the container, and the flowtriq, observe, local and flowspec plugins each augment it. The detect subtree decides that an attack is present, and a responder under one of those subtrees acts on the event. Detect a volumetric attack from the traffic Ze already sees. Detection is separate from mitigation: this container decides that an attack is happening and emits an event. A responder under flowspec or local is what acts on that event, and none is armed by default. Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline. Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline, default 5000. A quiet link cannot trigger on a small burst, because the threshold never falls under this value. Five times this value is also the packet-rate escape from startup-grace, so a rate over 25000 PPS triggers at the default while the grace period runs. Rolling baseline window size in samples. Rolling baseline window size in samples, and one sample is one evaluation, so one check-interval. The window p99 is recalculated every 10 admitted samples, so a cold detector runs on absolute-floor alone for its first 10 evaluations. A sample taken while the rate is over the threshold is refused, so an attack cannot raise the threshold that detects it. One sample in 3600 consecutive refused samples is admitted, which lets a lasting rise in traffic move the baseline. A persisted baseline is restored only when it carries 50 samples or more. Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert. Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert. The default is 50 Mbps. The value is expressed in bits/sec, which is the operator unit. The detector's internal rate is bytes/sec, and it converts the value. Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger. Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger. The trigger catches low-PPS, high-bandwidth amplification, such as NTP, memcached and CLDAP, that the packet-rate threshold misses. Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger beside the PPS threshold. Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger alongside the PPS threshold. When this leaf is false, only the packet-rate threshold can trigger detection. Run Stage-2 flow characterization on a detected attack. Run Stage-2 flow characterization. The stage classifies the family and the narrowest vector from the flow-export recent-flow ring, and emits AttackCharacterized. When this leaf is false, the detector still emits the coarse AttackDetected target from traffic-usage. Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger queries. Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger traffic-usage and flow-recent queries. On timeout, the detector falls back to the best available target. Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing an attack. Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing. Flows last seen before this window are ignored. Flows with no timestamp are always kept. Seconds between detection evaluations. Seconds between detection evaluations. Both rate feeds publish once a second: the traffic-statistics service, and the interface rate collector Ze falls back to when that service is absent. The detector folds this many samples and evaluates their PEAK, so a flood shorter than the interval still reaches the threshold. Every leaf that counts ticks against the threshold counts evaluations, so its wall-clock meaning is multiplied by this value. The default 1 evaluates every second. Consecutive evaluations below threshold before clearing. The count of consecutive evaluations under the threshold that ends an attack. The first one under the threshold moves an active detector to the clearing state and counts as the first check. The default 10 therefore holds the attack live for ten evaluations, which is ten seconds at the default check-interval. One evaluation back over the threshold returns the detector to active and drops the count. Consecutive evaluations above threshold before triggering. The count of consecutive evaluations over the threshold that arms the detector. One evaluation is check-interval seconds, one second at the default. The default 3 needs three unbroken evaluations over the threshold. A value of 0 or 1 triggers on the first one. One evaluation back under the threshold returns the detector to idle and restarts the count. Enable the DDoS detector. Enable the DDoS detector. Left false, the detector subscribes to no rate feed, so it takes no sample and its baseline stays cold. A commit rebuilds the detector and restores the persisted baseline either way, and the subscription is what this leaf controls. Source-address Shannon entropy in bits that marks an attack distributed. Source-address Shannon entropy (bits) at or above which an attack is logged as distributed or spoofed. A value of 0 is a single source, and a higher value is more sources. Allow and deny traffic policy applied to a detected attack. Allow/deny traffic policy applied to detected attacks, indexed by prefix. Ze evaluates the policy by longest-prefix match, where the most specific rule wins, and not by config order. The policy replaces the removed per-responder allowlists. The detector enforces it once and encodes the exempt or mitigate decision on the emitted event, so the responders obey it with no config read. Disposition when no rule matches the attack. Disposition when no rule matches. deny means defend, which is detection plus mitigation. allow means exempt from detection entirely. One allow or deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix. One allow/deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix. Precedence is longest-prefix match, so a /24 rule beats a covering /16 with no ordering. allow exempts matching traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling. allow exempts the matched traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling. The scope leaf decides how far each one reaches. allow at mitigation scope records the incident and installs no block, and allow at detection scope suppresses the incident. deny at detection scope also records without a block, and deny at mitigation scope is full handling. Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the destination, or either. Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the victim destination, or either. A source rule takes effect once the attack sources are characterized. Stage the action governs, mitigation or detection. Stage the action governs. mitigation means detect and record, and for allow it does not block. detection means that for allow the incident is suppressed entirely. Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger. Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger, default 90. The count follows the rate feed, one per second, so check-interval does not change it. A cold baseline warms during the grace period, and the grace stops that warm-up from firing on itself. Two things still trigger: a packet rate over five times absolute-floor, and the bandwidth trigger once its own baseline is ready. Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold. Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold. The threshold is the larger of two numbers: the window p99 multiplied by this leaf, and absolute-floor. The default 3.00 therefore triggers at three times the p99 of normal traffic. A changed value reaches the threshold at the next recalculation, which is within 10 admitted samples. Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume. Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume, default 10. Ties are broken by address. The same ranked list is what a source-matching policy rule reads, and every address in it has to fall inside the rule prefix before that rule matches. Answer a detected attack by announcing a BGP FlowSpec rule. The rule is announced to a peer, so the traffic is dropped upstream and never reaches this router. It needs a peer that accepts FlowSpec, which is what separates it from the local responder. FlowSpec traffic-action: discard or rate-limit. Mandatory, with no default. Neither discard nor rate-limit is universally safe, so this leaf has no default. discard announces an RFC 8955 traffic-rate of 0, which drops the characterized attack flow. rate-limit announces a byte rate, and it requires an explicit rate-limit-bytes. A rate-limit-bytes of 0 is a valid choice, and it is equivalent to discard on the wire. Maximum FlowSpec announcements per minute. The most FlowSpec announcements Ze sends in any 60 second window. An announcement over the limit is refused and logged, and the responder stays idle, so the next attack characterization inside the window announces nothing upstream and the one after the window rolls does. The limit protects the BGP sessions the rule goes to: a peer that drops the session over announce churn loses every rule it holds. 10 is the default, and the range is 1 to 600. Maximum hold-down after exponential backoff. Each probe that saturates doubles the current hold-down, and this value stops the doubling. Ze refuses a backoff-cap under hold-down, and the upper bound is 604800 seconds. 3600 is the default, which stops the wait at one hour. Announce an immediate upstream discard on a critical-severity AttackDetected. When true, a critical-severity AttackDetected (a peak of 5x the threshold or more) engages an immediate upstream discard, in the style of RTBH, and it does not wait for characterization. When false, the default, ze announces the upstream rule only from AttackCharacterized. The rule is then precise before the box goes blind behind the filter. Minimum incident confidence (0-100) to announce an upstream rule from a characterized attack. The default is 0, which accepts any confidence. The blackhole-fallback fast path never applies this minimum, because AttackDetected carries no confidence. Minimum seconds before the first leak-probe after announcement. The responder counts one second for each AttackOngoing event the detector emits, and the detector emits one for each traffic sample. The rule stays at full strength for this long, and the first leak-probe follows. A probe that saturates doubles the wait, up to backoff-cap. The range is 1 to 86400 seconds, and 300 is the default. Maximum seconds a FlowSpec rule stays announced (0 = no cap). The responder measures this against the wall clock, and not against the probe. An attack that goes quiet stops the AttackOngoing events the probe counts, which is the case the probe cannot see. 0 removes the cap, so the rule then stays until a probe withdraws it. 3600 is the default, and the range is 0 to 604800 seconds. Seconds between leak-probe attempts after hold-down. After the hold-down ends the responder waits this long. It then narrows the rule to probe-rate and watches what arrives. 60 is the default, and the range is 1 to 3600

ip-address port listener-port ui-mode enumeration Environment settings for API transports The api-server container under it is the shared parent of the REST and gRPC transports. ze-rest-conf and ze-grpc-conf merge their rest and grpc containers into it, so a transport compiled out leaves no container to configure. API engine settings (shared parent for the REST/gRPC transports) The token leaf here is shared by both transports. Each transport starts only when its own enabled leaf is true, or when ze.api-server.rest.enabled or ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts it. Ze parses the addresses, the CORS origin and the TLS pair even when the transport stays off. gRPC API transport. Authenticated non-loopback listeners require tls-cert and tls-key. A listen address that is not loopback must carry authentication and TLS, and Ze refuses to start the server without them. Without TLS the bearer token that gates each call crosses the network in clear. Ze accepts TLS 1.2 as its lowest version. Enable gRPC API server The default is false, so config starts no gRPC listener until the leaf is true. The environment variable ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts the transport with no leaf written. Ze parses the addresses and the TLS pair even when the transport stays off. gRPC API listen endpoints The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 50051, from the refine defaults under it. Listen IP address The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. On most services :: is dual-stack: it also accepts IPv4 clients, so :: alone serves both families. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and a dual-stack :: also overlaps every IPv4 address, so list :: alone rather than :: beside 0.0.0.0. A service whose IPv6 sockets are IPv6-only (L2TP, web) accepts :: beside an IPv4 address on the same port. Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses. Path to TLS certificate file for gRPC Write tls-cert and tls-key together. Ze refuses to start the server when one of the two is written and the other is not. Ze reads the pair from disk at start, so a path that names no file stops the server with an error. Path to TLS private key file for gRPC The leaf names the file that holds the private key of tls-cert, and Ze reads the two together at start. Ze marks the leaf ze:sensitive, so ze config dump prints the value $9$-encoded. REST and HTTP transport for the API server. A plain HTTP listener is restricted to loopback. To reach the API from another host, put a TLS terminator in front of the listener. CORS allowed origin (empty disables CORS headers) Ze copies the value into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header of each API answer, and validates nothing in it. An empty leaf sends no CORS header, and a preflight request then gets 204 with no header. A preflight answer permits GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and OPTIONS, permits the Authorization and Content-Type headers, and holds for 86400 seconds. Enable REST API server The default is false, so config starts no REST listener until the leaf is true. The environment variable ze.api-server.rest.enabled starts the transport with no leaf written. Ze parses the addresses and the CORS origin even when the transport stays off. REST API listen endpoints The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 8081, from the refine defaults under it. Listen IP address The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. On most services :: is dual-stack: it also accepts IPv4 clients, so :: alone serves both families. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family, and a dual-stack :: also overlaps every IPv4 address, so list :: alone rather than :: beside 0.0.0.0. A service whose IPv6 sockets are IPv6-only (L2TP, web) accepts :: beside an IPv4 address on the same port. Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and reports the one the host refuses. Bearer token for API authentication. When the token is set, a client MUST send the header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Leave the leaf empty to allow unauthenticated access. Backup workspace storage settings. Private working copies for uploaded backups and complete system backup downloads. The candidate directory is checked when the configuration is committed and becomes effective only after that commit succeeds. Existing workspaces and downloads remain in their original private folders until they close or expire. Absolute backup folder; apply after a successful commit. Absolute parent folder for private backup workspaces and download snapshots. The ze.backup.directory environment override takes priority. With no explicit setting, use the platform data directory's backups folder: the Linux and appliance data paths are resolved by the shared platform policy. A development binary with no recognized data directory keeps its operating-system temporary folder. Ze creates a missing parent folder and private children; it does not change an existing parent's mode or remove unrelated files. The daemon user must be able to create files here. A commit creates a missing folder and checks write permissions as the running daemon account. A failed commit keeps the previous effective folder. Existing private roots remain owned until their contents close or expire; empty retired roots are removed. Removing the leaf restores the platform default unless the OS override is set. BGP protocol environment settings, applied before any peer-level config. The container controls the OPEN wait timeout and the initial announce delay. Delay between reactor Ready and first UPDATE (duration, 0s-1h) The environment variable ze.bgp.announce.delay overrides the leaf. Ze holds every peer start for the delay after the reactor is otherwise Ready, which staggers route emission over a restart. Seconds to wait for peer OPEN after TCP connect The environment variable ze.bgp.openwait overrides the leaf. Ze arms the hold timer with the value after it sends OPEN. Ze resets that timer to the negotiated hold time when the peer OPEN arrives. BMP receiver settings The receiver starts only when enabled is true and the server list holds one entry at least. Ze stores each Route Monitoring message it accepts in the BMP RIB, and show bmp rib reads that RIB. Enable BMP receiver The default is false. The receiver needs this leaf true and one server entry at least, so enabled true on its own binds no address. Maximum concurrent BMP sessions The default is 100 and the range is 1 to 1000. The count is per listener, so two server entries admit twice this number of sessions. Over the limit Ze closes the new connection and logs a warning, and the sessions already open keep running. Action for received BMP Route Monitoring messages monitor is the default and the only value. The routes of a BMP Route Monitoring message go to the BMP RIB, which show bmp rib reads. They reach neither BGP best-path selection nor the FIB, because a BMP receiver is a monitoring station: RFC 7854 defines no use of the routes it is told about. Any other value is refused when the config loads. The leaf stays with one value on purpose: a value removed from the enumeration is refused, while a removed leaf would be skipped in silence. BMP receiver listen endpoints The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and address. Ze binds every added listener before removing any old listener. If a bind fails, startup or reload fails, added sockets close, and the listeners and session limit active before the attempt stay unchanged. An empty list binds nothing, because the receiver has no default endpoint. Listen IP address The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. On most services :: is dual-stack: it also accepts IPv4 clients, so :: alone serves both families.
